Summary
The letter describes a memorial service held in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, for Franklin D. Roosevelt, the late President of the United States and Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces. The service included an organ prelude, hymns, an invocation, a scripture reading, an address, a national anthem, and a recessional march. The service was organized by the US ASCOS (Army Service of the Chaplain) and featured various military personnel as participants.

AMEN. Lead, kindly Light, Amid th' encircling gloom, Lead Thou me on. The night is dark, And I am far away from home; Lead Thou me on. Keep Thou my feet; I do not ask to see The distant scene, One step enough for me. O say, can you see, by the dawn's early light, What so proudly we hailed at the twilight's last gleaming, Whose broad stripes and bright stars, through the perilous fight O'er the ramparts we watched were so gallantly streaming?
